sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa ordinary-passport visa-free regime replay
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA eVisa information page calls this same-origin session-bound endpoint with the selected passport-country identifier. In a retained fresh session, NZ=159, AU=14, CA=40, US=235, CL=45, AR=11, BR=31 and MX=143 each returned the direct Visa free regime Ordinary Passport value up to 30 days. CU=59 and SC=198 each returned no, which was not used to infer another route.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic MFA visa-free guidance: former-USSR bilateral agreements
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MFA consular page says its list covers all passport categories and places Cuba among countries governed by bilateral agreements between the former USSR and those states. The page metadata is last modified in 2020, so it documents the official waiver claim but does not by itself resolve present treaty force against the live selector.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa application form and controlling eligibility gate
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: The live MFA application form exposes country and Ordinary document choices, then its same-origin JavaScript posts doc_issued_by to getList7 before the later getVisaList_2 product-description call.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa controlling Tourist eligibility gate for Cuba and Seychelles
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: Fresh retained official-form sessions posted Cuba's exact country ID 59 and Seychelles' exact country ID 198. Each direct controlling response included the positive Tourist (TS) option before any product request.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa Ordinary Tourist result for Cuba and Seychelles
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: Only after the respective positive getList7 gates, the same fresh sessions sent ids=56, doc_type=1 (Ordinary), visa_filtr=1 (Single Entry) and service_level=2 for Cuba ID 59 and Seychelles ID 198. Both direct results describe Tourist TS issuance for tourism up to 30 days.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Tourist visa («TS») is issued to an applicant, intending to visit Kyrgyz Republic with purpose of tourism, for a period up to 30 days.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa information: electronic confirmation before entry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Kyrgyz Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA's current eVisa information page says applicants complete an online application and enter after receiving eVisa confirmation through the portal, which establishes electronic issuance before travel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: After receiving your e-Visa confirmation through this portal, you can enter the Kyrgyz Republic during e-Visa validity period.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa service terms: electronic-visa checkpoints
sources.officialityEvidence: The current eVisa service terms identify the Government of Kyrgyzstan as making the service available and specify the permitted points of entry for electronic visas received through the portal.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Electronic visa, received via this portal, can be used only if you travel via Manas International Airport, Osh International Airport, Ak-dzol checkpoint.

sources.title: Seychelles Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa guidance
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Diaspora
sources.officialityEvidence: The currently accessible Seychelles MFA page lists Kyrgyzstan in its current interface headed “List of countries that Seychellois passport holders require visa.” It does not identify an issuing channel, so it is only reconciled with Kyrgyzstan's direct eVisa result rather than used to infer mission issuance.

policies.title: Eight ordinary passports: direct 30-day visa-free regime
policies.summary: The current MFA nationality-regime endpoint directly returns Visa free regime, Ordinary Passport: up to 30 days for each listed passport-country ID.
conditions: Fresh retained-session direct regime replays used NZ=159, AU=14, CA=40, US=235, CL=45, AR=11, BR=31 and MX=143. Each returned Visa free regime with the Ordinary Passport value up to 30 days.
The endpoint also displayed a separate facilitated-visa label for these rows. That label is not normalized as visa on arrival, eVisa, a longer stay or another route.
This covers the ordinary-passport short-visitor baseline only; work, residence, registration, transit, diplomatic/service/special documents, security and individual admission remain separate.

policies.title: Seychelles ordinary passports: Kyrgyz Republic Tourist eVisa
policies.summary: For Seychelles, the current MFA eVisa application's controlling getList7 gate directly offered Tourist (TS). The resulting Ordinary Tourist response is issued for tourism up to 30 days, and the portal requires eVisa confirmation before entry.
conditions: A fresh retained application session selected Seychelles=198. Its direct getList7 response positively included Tourist (TS) before a Tourist product was requested.

Only after that positive gate, the Ordinary replay used ids=56, doc_type=1, visa_filtr=1 (Single Entry) and service_level=2. The response says Tourist visa (TS) is issued for tourism for a period up to 30 days and cannot be issued while the foreign national is in Kyrgyzstan.

Complete and pay the online application, then receive eVisa confirmation through the portal before entry. The form labels service level 2 as consideration within 2 business days; that is expedited consideration, not a guaranteed standard decision time.

The electronic visa is usable only through Manas International Airport, Osh International Airport or Ak-dzol checkpoint. Work, residence, transit, diplomatic/service/special-document, security and individual-admission decisions remain outside this ordinary short-visitor policy.

The current Seychelles MFA interface says Seychellois passport holders need a visa for Kyrgyzstan, but does not specify a mission-only route or issuance channel. The direct Kyrgyz MFA electronic eligibility and issuance results therefore establish the pre-travel eVisa route.

application.label: Kyrgyz Republic eVisa application
application.processingTime: The live form offers expedited “Consideration of the application within 2 business days”; it does not promise a standard decision time.
steps: Before travel, select Seychelles, Ordinary travel document and the positive Tourist (TS) option in the MFA eVisa form.
Complete and pay the electronic application, then receive eVisa confirmation through the portal before travel.
Use the confirmed eVisa through Manas International Airport, Osh International Airport or Ak-dzol checkpoint, subject to normal admission checks.

conflicts.explanation: Seychelles guidance says a visa is needed but does not establish a mission-only channel. A fresh official application session directly returned Tourist (TS) at Seychelles ID 198's controlling gate and the subsequent Ordinary Tourist result says the visa is issued for tourism up to 30 days; portal confirmation is required before entry.

unresolved.reason: Current official sources disagree and their hierarchy cannot be resolved from currently accessible primary law. The live MFA consular guidance still places Cuba in the former-USSR bilateral all-passport waiver group, and the canonical Export Agency guidance reviewed on 2026-08-21 also names Cuba visa-free; however, the fresh session-bound MFA nationality endpoint returned Visa free regime / Ordinary Passport: no. Cuba's positive Tourist gate and Ordinary Tourist product do not resolve this: a directly confirmed waiver passport, New Zealand, produced the same positive gate and product in the same controlled replay, so portal eVisa availability cannot displace a waiver. No current primary treaty-status text, amendment, suspension or authoritative hierarchy was recovered; the Export host was DNS-unavailable and the Cabinet legal portal was inaccessible through its trusted TLS path. Cuba is therefore held rather than classified as eVisa or silently retaining the waiver.
